note.question: What determines the placement, delivery promise, and fulfillment decisions of an online retailer?
note.overview: The model considers the placement, delivery promise, and fulfillment decisions of an online retailer. We have a set of products with given numbers of units to be placed at capacitated fulfillment centers. Once we make the placement decisions, we face demands for the products arriving from different demand regions randomly over time.

source.quote: We consider the placement, delivery promise, and fulfillment decisions of an online retailer.

If we offer delivery promise k to a demand for product a in demand region j, then the customer accepts the promise with probability θa jk, in which case, if we use fulfillment center i to serve this demand, then we generate a profit of ra ijk.

Our goal is to decide how many units of each product to place at each fulfillment center at the beginning of the selling horizon and which delivery promise and fulfill­ ment center to use to serve each demand over the selling horizon so that we maximize the total expected profit.
Organization In Section 2, we formulate the joint placement, delivery promise, and fulfillment problem.
The retailer chooses the delivery promise to offer to a customer, in response to which, the customer decides whether to make a purchase.
In this way, each fulfillment center faces an exogenous demand stream.
In our model, for each product a, we focus on placing the total amount of Ca units, which has been dictated by the national target inventory level.

conditions: Considering the case in which the placement decisions for product a are given by the vector ˆza, we use ˆzmin = mini∈F{ˆza i : ˆza i ≥1} to capture the smallest nonzero placement quantity for the product at any fulfillment center.
In our policy, we solve the Bounding problem with za = ˆza once at the beginning of the selling horizon.
Throughout this section, we proceed with the understanding that the placement decisions ˆza are fixed and focus on constructing the delivery promise and fulfillment policy.

components.formal: Decision rule: In contrast, the randomized policy may assign a demand to a fulfillment center without any remaining inventory even when there are other fulfillment centers with remaining inventories.
conditions: If the placement decisions of product a are given ˆza, then the total expected profit of the randomized policy from product a is P i∈FVa i1( ˆza i ).
To perform a rollout on the randomized policy, we replace Ja t+1(xa) in the Fulfillment dynamic program with P i∈FVa i,t+1(xa i ) and solve the corresponding maximization problem.
It is known that the rollout policy performs at least as well as the initial policy on hand; see section 6.1.3 in Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis (1996).
